evidence: Hor. S. 1.1.106: est modus in rēbus, sunt certī dēnique fīnēs
terms.comment: Literally “there is a measure in things”.
Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections, checked against the editions named there.
